AutoMountDrives.Description: Finds every fixed internal partition with a mountable filesystem (ext4/btrfs/xfs/f2fs/ntfs/exfat/vfat) that isn't already handled, and adds a permanent /etc/fstab entry mounting it at a stable /mnt/<label> path with 'nofail' — the right place for a second games/data NVMe, so Steam libraries and symlinks never move. Skips the OS/boot/swap disks, anything already in fstab, LUKS, and removable media. NTFS uses the in-kernel ntfs3 driver with your uid/gid so games are writable. Reversible: undo unmounts and strips exactly the block it added (and migrates off any older /run/media setup a previous version made).

CstateFix.Description: Adds processor.max_cstate=1 to the kernel boot params. The 5800H's deep C-states (C6) are unstable on this board and cause random full-system freezes. Requires reboot to take effect.

IdleNomwait.Description: Alternative to the C-state fix above — skips the mwait idle driver entirely. Try this INSTEAD of the C-state fix if that one doesn't resolve freezes, not in addition to it. Requires reboot.

ClocksourceTsc.Description: Forces the CPU's own timestamp counter instead of the motherboard's HPET as the system timer. Helps timing jitter on some boards, does nothing on others. Requires reboot.

UsbAutosuspend.Description: Stops Linux from power-suspending USB ports, fixing wireless mouse/controller dongles or headsets that lag or briefly disconnect.

MouseAccelFlat.Description: 1:1 mouse movement, no acceleration curve — applies under X11. Under Wayland/KDE Plasma (Nobara's default) also set System Settings > Mouse > Acceleration Profile to Flat.
apply:
printf 'Section "InputClass"
    Identifier "Flat pointer accel"
    MatchIsPointer "on"
    Driver "libinput"
    Option "AccelProfile" "flat"
    Option "AccelSpeed" "0"
EndSection
' > /etc/X11/xorg.conf.d/50-mouse-accel.conf

Swappiness.Description: Keeps RAM from being swapped out while games/mods are open. Pairs well with the zram tweak below.

ZramTune.Description: Fedora/Nobara already runs zram-generator by default — this bumps its size fraction for heavier gaming loads.

BalooDisable.Description: Stops background file content indexing — the single biggest idle CPU/disk drain on stock Plasma. Applied for your user account.

PowerProfileScripts.Description: Two one-word commands that emulate the Windows G-key: 'gaming-performance' sets the 'performance' platform_profile (= G-Mode: firmware ramps the fan curve + raises CPU/GPU power limits) AND slams the alienware-wmi fan boost to max, like AWCC does; 'gaming-balanced' undoes both. These are what the tray icon, the G-key listener and the Dashboard toggle call.
apply:
cat > /usr/local/bin/gaming-performance <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
powerprofilesctl set performance
# G-Mode fan slam (AWCC-style): max the alienware-wmi fan boost
for h in /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*; do
  [ "$(cat "$h/name" 2>/dev/null)" = alienware_wmi ] || continue
  for b in "$h"/fan[0-9]*_boost; do [ -w "$b" ] && echo 255 > "$b"; done
done
exit 0
SCRIPT

cat > /usr/local/bin/gaming-balanced <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
powerprofilesctl set balanced
for h in /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*; do
  [ "$(cat "$h/name" 2>/dev/null)" = alienware_wmi ] || continue
  for b in "$h"/fan[0-9]*_boost; do [ -w "$b" ] && echo 0 > "$b"; done
done
exit 0
SCRIPT

TlpEnable.Description: Mature laptop power/thermal tuning for the 5800H. Disables power-profiles-daemon to avoid the two fighting over the CPU governor. Pick this OR the auto-cpufreq app below, not both.

AmdgpuPerfScripts.Description: Forces the AMD Vega iGPU to its highest DPM performance level on demand (Linux equivalent of disabling AMD ULPS on Windows). Only matters if you're rendering on the iGPU.

NvidiaMaxPerf.Description: Enables NVIDIA persistence mode + prefers max PowerMizer performance, avoiding clock-transition stutter at the cost of power/heat. Run it before a session.
apply:
printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash
nvidia-smi -pm 1 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
if [[ -n "${DISPLAY:-}" ]] && command -v nvidia-settings >/dev/null; then nvidia-settings -a "[gpu:0]/GpuPowerMizerMode=1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
exit 0
' > /usr/local/bin/nvidia-max-perf

ControllerUdev.Description: Non-root access to Xbox/PlayStation/generic HID pads. Usually already covered by the Steam package — this is a fallback.
apply:
printf 'SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTRS{idVendor}=="045e", MODE="0666"
SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTRS{idVendor}=="054c", MODE="0666"
SUBSYSTEM=="hidraw", MODE="0666"
' > /etc/udev/rules.d/99-gamepads.rules

HotkeyListener.Description: Installs a systemd user service that listens for the dedicated G-key (confirmed on the G15 5515 to send KEY_PERFORMANCE when Fn Lock is OFF) and toggles Game Mode on press — same effect as clicking the tray icon. Requires PowerProfileScripts/AmdgpuPerfScripts/NvidiaMaxPerf above to be installed first, and python3-evdev. Adds your user to the 'input' group so the service can read the keyboard device — log out and back in once after applying for that to take effect.
HotkeyListener.check: sudo -u {USER} XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u {USER}) systemctl --user is-enabled tuxthrottle-hotkey.service 2>/dev/null | grep -q enabled && id -nG {USER} | grep -qw input
undo: sudo -u {USER} XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u {USER}) systemctl --user disable --now tuxthrottle-hotkey.service 2>/dev/null || true

PasswordlessGameModeToggle.Description: Lets the tray icon and the G-key listener flip Game Mode without a password prompt every single press. Scoped ONLY to the five specific toggle scripts, not general root access. Skip this if you'd rather approve each toggle via a GUI polkit prompt.

RaplPowerPermissions.Description: Linux locks CPU package power counters (RAPL, under /sys/class/powercap) to root-only by default since 2020 (a side-channel security mitigation) — without this, the Dashboard tab and the tray icon (which deliberately run unprivileged) can never show real CPU wattage, always 'n/a'. Adds a udev rule making them world-readable, the same fix MangoHud's own docs recommend for its power display. Note: Nobara 43 already ships these files world-readable, so this is usually a no-op there — apply it only if the Dashboard actually shows 'n/a' for CPU wattage. Trade-off: makes RAPL energy counters readable by any local user/process, a known but low-severity timing side-channel — standard practice on gaming-focused distros/tools, not enabled by default here.

MangoHudGlobalToggle.Description: Turns MangoHud into a system-wide overlay instead of something you paste into each game's Steam launch options one at a time. Installs 'mangohud-global-on'/'mangohud-global-off', which write/remove ~/.config/environment.d/mangohud.conf with just MANGOHUD=1 — Vulkan games pick up the overlay via the implicit-layer 'enable_environment' mechanism from that alone. NO global LD_PRELOAD: an LD_PRELOAD of libMangoHud.so forces the overlay layer into KWin and Plasma too, and editing the MangoHud config from this app then crashes the desktop session (KWin SIGABRT, tray loses the power/battery applets). Takes effect on next login since it's a systemd environment.d file, not a live env var. Once active, MangoHud's own in-game keybind (Shift_R+F12 by default) shows/hides the overlay. Requires the GameModeMangoHud app installed first.
apply:
cat > /usr/local/bin/mangohud-global-on <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/environment.d
cat > ~/.config/environment.d/mangohud.conf <<'CONF'
MANGOHUD=1
CONF
echo 'MangoHud enabled globally (MANGOHUD=1, no LD_PRELOAD) - log out/in for it to apply to new games.'
SCRIPT

cat > /usr/local/bin/mangohud-global-off <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
rm -f ~/.config/environment.d/mangohud.conf
echo 'MangoHud global toggle removed - log out/in (or relaunch Steam) for it to fully clear.'
SCRIPT

KernelGamingCmdline.Description: Adds a curated, hardware-appropriate subset of the usual gaming kernel cmdline: split_lock_detect=off + split_lock_mitigate=0 (no stalls on misaligned locked ops — common in games/emulators), nowatchdog + nosoftlockup (drop the per-second watchdog timer/IRQ), timer_migration=0 (keep timers on their own CPU), preempt=full (fully preemptible — this Nobara kernel is PREEMPT_DYNAMIC so it takes the switch), threadirqs (threaded IRQ handlers, better audio/input latency), ignore_rlimit_data (some Wine/DXVK builds need it), sysrq_always_enabled=1, audit=0. Deliberately EXCLUDES the Intel-only / laptop-dangerous entries from typical desktop lists (intel_pstate=disable is a no-op on this AMD CPU; thermal.off=1, nomce, vdso=0, nohz_full=all left out on purpose). Requires reboot.
apply: grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="sysrq_always_enabled=1 split_lock_detect=off split_lock_mitigate=0 nowatchdog nosoftlockup timer_migration=0 preempt=full threadirqs ignore_rlimit_data audit=0"
undo: grubby --update-kernel=ALL --remove-args="sysrq_always_enabled=1 split_lock_detect=off split_lock_mitigate=0 nowatchdog nosoftlockup timer_migration=0 preempt=full threadirqs ignore_rlimit_data audit=0"

Ipv6DisableCmdline.Description: Adds ipv6.disable=1 to the kernel cmdline — matches the setup this config was ported from. Only do this if you know nothing on your network needs IPv6 (some VPNs, Tailscale MagicDNS, and a few games' matchmaking prefer it). Requires reboot.

CpuMaxPerformance.Content: Force CPU performance governor at boot
CpuMaxPerformance.Description: Installs a oneshot systemd service (tuxthrottle-cpu-perf.service) that pins every core to the 'performance' governor and energy_performance_preference=performance on boot — the amd_pstate 'active' driver on the 5800H only exposes performance/powersave, so this is the max-clocks setting. NOTE: power-profiles-daemon rewrites the governor whenever you switch power profile (or use the Game Mode toggle), so this mainly helps if you do NOT switch profiles / don't use Game Mode. If you use Game Mode, that already covers it. Reversible.
apply:
cat > /usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-cpu-perf <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
for f in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor; do echo performance > "$f"; done
for f in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/energy_performance_preference; do [ -e "$f" ] && echo performance > "$f"; done
SCRIPT

cat > /etc/systemd/system/tuxthrottle-cpu-perf.service <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=Force CPU performance governor (TuxThrottle)
After=multi-user.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-cpu-perf

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT

BtrfsNoatime.Description: Stops the filesystem writing an access-time stamp on every file read — pure I/O reduction, safe on Btrfs (Nobara's default). Backs up /etc/fstab to /etc/fstab.tuxthrottle-bak first, edits only the ' / ' Btrfs line, and remounts live. Undo restores the backup.

NvmeIoTune.Description: The NVMe scheduler is already 'none' on this system (correct for NVMe), so this only lowers read_ahead_kb to 128 (from 256) — less wasted prefetch on the small random reads typical of game assets. Tiny effect, fully reversible. (nr_requests is left alone: its max is per-device and some queues here reject a bump, which just logs a harmless udev error at boot.)

WifiPowersaveOff.Description: The AX200 has power-save ON by default, which adds latency spikes and occasional stutter to online play. Writes a NetworkManager drop-in (wifi.powersave=2) so it stays off across reconnects. Reversible.
apply: systemctl reload NetworkManager || systemctl restart NetworkManager || true

NetLatencySysctl.Description: Writes /etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxthrottle-net.conf: BBR congestion control + fq qdisc (better behaviour under load / on lossy Wi-Fi), TCP Fast Open, no slow-start-after-idle, bigger backlog and socket buffers. All stock kernel features on Nobara. Reversible.

DnfSpeed.Description: Appends max_parallel_downloads=10 and fastestmirror=True to /etc/dnf/dnf.conf — the dnf equivalent of ranking mirrors. Makes every install/update in this toolkit noticeably faster. Reversible (removes the two lines).

GamingResourceLimits.Description: Wine (esync/fsync), Proton, and shader compilers open huge numbers of file descriptors and memory maps. Sets a hard/soft nofile limit of 1048576 in /etc/security/limits.d and bumps fs.file-max, fs.inotify.max_user_watches, and vm.max_map_count via sysctl. Takes effect on next login for the nofile limit. Reversible.

KbdBacklightFix.Content: Keyboard Backlight: re-apply saved colour at boot/resume
KbdBacklightFix.Description: On the G15 5515 the keyboard backlight is driven through OpenRGB (the AW-ELC has no kernel driver and ignores raw HID writes); the backlight must also be enabled in BIOS setup. This installs tuxthrottle_kbd.py (an openrgb wrapper) to /usr/local/bin, a headless 'openrgb --server' service so colour changes apply in ~1s instead of ~4s, plus a systemd service + a systemd-sleep hook that re-apply ~/.config/tuxthrottle/kbd.json (set in the Keyboard tab) at boot and after resume, since the colour does not persist a power cycle on its own. Requires the OpenRGB app. Reversible.
KbdBacklightFix.check: test -x /usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-kbd && systemctl is-enabled tuxthrottle-kbd.service 2>/dev/null | grep -q enabled && systemctl is-enabled tuxthrottle-openrgb.service 2>/dev/null | grep -q enabled
apply:
cat > /etc/systemd/system/tuxthrottle-openrgb.service <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=OpenRGB SDK server for the Dell G15 keyboard (TuxThrottle)
After=multi-user.target systemd-udev-settle.service

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/bin/openrgb --server --noautoconnect
ExecStartPost=/bin/sh -c 'for i in $(seq 40); do ss -ltn 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":6742 " && break; sleep 0.5; done; exit 0'
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=3
TimeoutStartSec=40

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT

cat > /etc/systemd/system/tuxthrottle-kbd.service <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=Re-apply Dell G15 keyboard backlight (TuxThrottle)
After=multi-user.target systemd-udev-settle.service tuxthrottle-openrgb.service
Wants=tuxthrottle-openrgb.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
Environment=TUXTHROTTLE_KBD_STATE=/home/{USER}/.config/tuxthrottle/kbd.json
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-kbd apply-saved
TimeoutStartSec=150

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT

cat > /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/tuxthrottle-kbd <<'HOOK'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "$1" = post ]; then
  sleep 2
  TUXTHROTTLE_KBD_STATE=/home/{USER}/.config/tuxthrottle/kbd.json /usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-kbd apply-saved || true
fi
HOOK

RyzenAdjTDP.Content: CPU TDP control (ryzenadj) + persist across reboot
RyzenAdjTDP.Description: Installs ryzenadj (from the distro repo, or built from source as a fallback) so the Power & Limits tab can set the 5800H's STAPM / fast / slow power limits — the Linux 'ThrottleStop for Ryzen'. Also installs tuxthrottle-tdp (re-applies ~/.config/tuxthrottle/tdp.json), a boot+resume service so your chosen limits survive a reboot, and a narrow sudoers rule so a future CLI/tray can call it without a password. cat > /usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-tdp <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Apply STAPM/fast/slow limits from tdp.json (Watts). Usage: tuxthrottle-tdp [file]
set -e
RA="$(command -v ryzenadj || echo /usr/local/bin/ryzenadj)"
F="${1:-/home/{USER}/.config/tuxthrottle/tdp.json}"
[ -r "$F" ] || { echo "no $F"; exit 0; }
read_key(){ grep -oE "\"$1\"[ ]*:[ ]*[0-9]+" "$F" | grep -oE '[0-9]+$'; }
S=$(read_key stapm); FA=$(read_key fast); SL=$(read_key slow)
ARGS=()
[ -n "$S" ]  && ARGS+=(--stapm-limit=$((S*1000)))
[ -n "$FA" ] && ARGS+=(--fast-limit=$((FA*1000)))
[ -n "$SL" ] && ARGS+=(--slow-limit=$((SL*1000)))
[ ${#ARGS[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo 'nothing to apply'; exit 0; }
exec "$RA" "${ARGS[@]}"
SCRIPT

This is what lets the waybar / KDE-plasmoid profile buttons switch the power profile on their own. Remote / ssh / inactive sessions still require admin auth (allow_any/allow_inactive = auth_admin). It is a plain .policy file in /usr/share/polkit-1/actions/ — NOT a D-Bus bus policy — so it can't wedge the system bus; polkitd simply ignores a file it can't parse. The apply step verifies the action loaded (pkaction) and rolls itself back if polkit rejected it. Reversible — undo removes the file and reloads polkit.

NvidiaShaderCache.Content: NVIDIA: stop shader-cache pruning (kills the every-launch recompile)
NvidiaShaderCache.Description: The NVIDIA Linux driver prunes its shader disk cache between sessions, so many games do a FULL shader recompile on every launch — 100% CPU for 10–15 min and stutter until it finishes. Drops env vars into /etc/environment.d/ that give the cache a large fixed budget and disable the cleanup pass (__GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE=1, ..._PATH, ..._SIZE, ..._SKIP_CLEANUP=1). The path + size come from the Setup Games → “Shader / pipeline cache storage” box (~/.config/tuxthrottle/shadercache.json) if you've set one, else ~/.cache/tuxthrottle-shaders/nv-shader-cache at 80 GB. Re-apply this tweak after changing that location. Takes effect on next login. Reversible.
apply: CFG=/home/{USER}/.config/tuxthrottle/shadercache.json; D=$(grep -oE '"dir"[ ]*:[ ]*"[^"]+"' "$CFG" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/.*:[ ]*"//; s/"$//'); D=${D:-/home/{USER}/.cache/tuxthrottle-shaders}; case "$D" in "~/"*) D=/home/{USER}/${D#\~/} ;; "~") D=/home/{USER} ;; esac; G=$(grep -oE '"max_size_gb"[ ]*:[ ]*[0-9]+' "$CFG" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+$'); G=${G:-80}; NVDIR="$D/nv-shader-cache"; install -d -o {USER} -g {USER} "$NVDIR"; printf '%s\n' '# TuxThrottle: keep the NVIDIA shader disk cache instead of recompiling every launch' '__GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE=1' "__GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_PATH=$NVDIR" "__GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_SIZE=$((G*1000000000))" '__GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_SKIP_CLEANUP=1' > /etc/environment.d/90-tuxthrottle-nv-shadercache.conf

NvidiaDynamicBoost.Description: nvidia-powerd arbitrates the shared CPU/GPU power budget on Ryzen+RTX laptops (Dynamic Boost). If it isn't running the dGPU is capped near its base clock and you lose a chunk of gaming performance. Enables + starts nvidia-powerd.service (ships with the NVIDIA driver). Reversible.

SplitLockMitigateOff.Content: Disable split-lock detection (removes a big stall penalty in some games)
SplitLockMitigateOff.Description: The kernel's split-lock detector stalls a thread hard (tens of ms) whenever a misaligned locked memory op crosses a cache line — a pattern some games / anti-cheats hit, costing 20–40% FPS. Sets kernel.split_lock_mitigate=0 via /etc/sysctl.d/, applied now and at boot. Only matters on CPUs that support split-lock detection (Intel Tremont+, AMD Zen 4+) — a harmless no-op on the Ryzen 7 5800H (Zen 3), which has no such sysctl. No downside on a personal gaming machine. Reversible.

SchedExtGaming.Content: sched-ext: run the scx_lavd low-latency scheduler (Steam Deck's)
SchedExtGaming.Description: Installs scx-scheds and runs scx_lavd --performance — the sched_ext scheduler Valve ships on the Steam Deck, tuned for low frame-time variance under gaming load. Needs kernel 6.12+ with sched_ext (Nobara/Fedora 43+ has it). Runs as tuxthrottle-scx.service (also at boot). CAVEAT: on some kernels (seen on Nobara 7.2 with scx_lavd 1.1.3) scx_lavd starves systemd kworkers and the sched_ext stall watchdog kills it every 1–3 min, and a compositor caught in one of those 30 s stalls can crash the KDE session (power management vanishes). Guards: the unit is capped at 3 restarts / 2 min, and Apply watches 75 s after enabling — if scx_lavd stalls in that window it backs itself out completely and leaves you on the stable stock scheduler (Apply reports failure). The kernel also reverts to its default scheduler the instant the service stops. Reversible, no reboot. **CONFIRMED to hard-freeze this Dell G15 on kernel 7.2 — do not enable.** If scx keeps coming back after undo, Nobara's own on-demand loader is the cause: `sudo systemctl disable --now --mask scx_loader.service`. Not in any preset; never marked recommended.

for k in $(seq 1 25); do [ -e /sys/kernel/sched_ext/root/ops ] && break; sleep 1; done

[ -e /sys/kernel/sched_ext/root/ops ] || { echo 'TuxThrottle: scx_lavd did not attach in 25s — see journalctl -u tuxthrottle-scx'; systemctl disable --now tuxthrottle-scx.service 2>/dev/null; rm -f /etc/systemd/system/tuxthrottle-scx.service; systemctl daemon-reload; exit 1; }

echo 'TuxThrottle: scx_lavd attached — watching 75s for the sched_ext stall watchdog (some kernels starve kworkers under scx_lavd)…'; _n0=$(systemctl show tuxthrottle-scx.service -p NRestarts --value); sleep 75; _n1=$(systemctl show tuxthrottle-scx.service -p NRestarts --value); if [ "$_n1" != "$_n0" ] || ! systemctl is-active --quiet tuxthrottle-scx.service || ! [ -e /sys/kernel/sched_ext/root/ops ]; then echo 'TuxThrottle: scx_lavd stalled on this kernel (sched_ext runnable-task-stall watchdog) — backing out, leaving you on the stable stock scheduler. KWin only tears for apps that explicitly ask (tearing-control protocol / Vulkan immediate present); everything else is unaffected. Reversible.

Adds acpi_backlight=nvidia_wmi_ec to the kernel command line (grubby, all kernels), restoring brightness control via the NVIDIA WMI EC interface. ONLY apply if your brightness control is actually broken; needs a reboot. Reversible.

AmdPstateActive.Description: amd_pstate has three modes; 'active' (EPP-driven) is what lets Cezanne (Ryzen 7 5800H) boost properly and follow the platform power profile. Adds amd_pstate=active to the kernel command line if it isn't already the running mode. No-op where the kernel already defaults to active (recent Fedora/Nobara). Needs a reboot. Reversible.

DellBatteryThreshold.Description: The G15 5515 has no kernel charge_control_end_threshold, but Dell firmware supports a 'custom' charge interval stored in NVRAM. This installs libsmbios (smbios-battery-ctl); the Power & Limits tab then sets the stop-charging percentage through it and it persists in firmware across reboots — no service needed. Undo removes the package only; any interval you set stays in firmware until you set it back to 100 %/standard.

NvidiaRuntimePM.Content: NVIDIA: fine-grained runtime power management (dGPU D3cold when idle)
NvidiaRuntimePM.Description: Sets the nvidia module option NVreg_DynamicPowerManagement=0x02 so the RTX 3050 Ti fully powers down (D3cold) whenever nothing is using it — it frees its ~40 MiB of VRAM and ~5 W, and wakes automatically for a PRIME-offloaded game or DaVinci Resolve. Without it the dGPU idles 'active' the whole session. Writes /etc/modprobe.d/tuxthrottle-nvidia-rtd3.conf and rebuilds the initramfs; needs a reboot. Reversible.

KernelUltraCmdline.Content: Kernel Boot Params: aggressive extras (mitigations off, PCIe/NVMe latency)
KernelUltraCmdline.Description: The spicier kernel cmdline args the curated set deliberately leaves out — opt in only if you want max speed and accept the trade-offs. mitigations=off (drops ALL CPU speculative-execution mitigations — ~5–15% back in syscall/scheduler-heavy workloads on this Zen 3; you lose Spectre/Meltdown/Retbleed protection, fine on a single-user gaming box, NOT on a shared/work machine). nvme_core.default_ps_max_latency_us=0 (disables NVMe APST power-saving — lower I/O latency AND fixes the APST dropout bug this ADATA IM2P33F3 SSD is prone to). pcie_aspm=off (no PCIe link power management — lower latency to the dGPU/NVMe, more power + heat). amdgpu.ppfeaturemask=0xffffffff (unlocks the iGPU PowerPlay table so CoreCtrl/LACT can tune it). iommu=pt (IOMMU in passthrough mode — near-zero DMA-translation overhead, protection kept for non-passthrough devices). zswap.enabled=0 (turn off zswap — it and zram both running is redundant; zram wins). Requires reboot. Reversible.

VmWritebackSysctl.Content: VM writeback + reclaim sysctls (no flush hitches)
VmWritebackSysctl.Description: Writes /etc/sysctl.d/99-tuxthrottle-vm.conf. Bounds dirty-page writeback to 320 MB / 128 MB (dirty_bytes / dirty_background_bytes) instead of the % default, so a big buffered write can't build up hundreds of MB and then stall the game when the kernel flushes it. page-cluster=0 (best with zram — no read-ahead on swap-in). watermark_scale_factor=125 + watermark_boost_factor=0 (kick background reclaim earlier and don't over-reclaim, avoiding sudden allocation stalls under memory pressure). Applied now and at boot. Reversible.

NvidiaAggressiveModule.Content: NVIDIA: aggressive module options (PAT, no mem-zeroing, ReBAR, max PowerMizer)
NvidiaAggressiveModule.Description: Writes /etc/modprobe.d/99-tuxthrottle-nvidia-aggr.conf and rebuilds the initramfs (reboot needed). NVreg_UsePageAttributeTable=1 (write-combined CPU mappings of GPU memory — faster CPU→GPU transfers, a long-standing free win). NVreg_InitializeSystemMemoryAllocations=0 (don't pre-zero system memory handed to the GPU — quicker allocations; minor info-leak-between-your-own-processes trade). NVreg_EnableResizableBar=1 (ask the driver to use Resizable BAR if the platform allows any window — no-op if not). NVreg_RegistryDwords PowerMizer set to force maximum performance level while on AC — the dGPU holds high clocks instead of ramping. RUNS THE GPU HOTTER: the G15's cooling is already marginal, watch temps; pair with the aggressive fan curve. requires an NVIDIA GPU. Reversible.

GpuGamingEnv.Content: GPU gaming env vars (RADV GPL, glthread, NVIDIA threaded/low-latency)
GpuGamingEnv.Description: Writes /etc/environment.d/95-tuxthrottle-gpu-gaming.conf (takes effect next login). RADV_PERFTEST=gpl,nggc,sam (graphics-pipeline-library = far less in-game shader stutter on the AMD iGPU, NGG culling, Smart Access Memory path). mesa_glthread=true (offload GL calls to a worker thread — big win for CPU-bound OpenGL titles). __GL_THREADED_OPTIMIZATIONS=1 (same for the NVIDIA GL driver). __GL_YIELD=USLEEP (sleep instead of busy-spinning while waiting on the GPU — frees a core). __GL_MaxFramesAllowed=2 (cap the render-ahead queue — lower input lag; set to 1 for the absolute minimum at some FPS cost). __GL_VRR_ALLOWED=1 (let G-Sync/VRR engage). Reversible.

ServiceMaskGaming.Content: Mask idle background services (CUPS, Avahi, ModemManager, SSSD, updatedb)
ServiceMaskGaming.Description: Masks daemons that do nothing on a personal gaming laptop but still wake up, poll, and hold RAM: cups (printing), avahi-daemon (mDNS/Bonjour discovery), ModemManager (there's no modem), sssd + sssd-kcm (enterprise auth — unused off a domain), and the plocate-updatedb.timer (the weekly whole-disk index scan). Frees a bit of RAM and stops the periodic CPU/I-O blips. `undo` unmasks them. Skip this if you actually print or use network file-share discovery.

systemctl mask cups.service cups.socket cups.path avahi-daemon.service avahi-daemon.socket ModemManager.service sssd.service sssd-kcm.socket plocate-updatedb.timer 2>/dev/null || true

AnanicyCpp.Content: ananicy-cpp: auto nice / ionice / scheduling rules
AnanicyCpp.Description: Installs and enables ananicy-cpp — a lightweight daemon that applies per-process priority rules from a shipped ruleset: games and the compositor get a better nice level, real-time scheduling where safe, and idle-class I/O for background junk (trackers, updaters, compilers). IrqThreadsRt.Content: Real-time priority for GPU / NVMe IRQ threads (RISKY)
IrqThreadsRt.Description: The curated cmdline already turns hardware IRQ handlers into kernel threads (threadirqs). This gives the amdgpu, nvidia and nvme IRQ threads SCHED_FIFO real-time priority (50 for the GPUs, 45 for NVMe) so a fully-loaded CPU can never delay a GPU-done or storage-complete interrupt — smoother frame pacing under CPU load. **RISK: real-time IRQ scheduling has bitten this machine — under any scheduler stress (an alt scheduler stalling, a driver hiccup, an I/O-hung disk) an RT IRQ thread can monopolise a CPU and freeze the box. Advanced / experiment only; not in any preset; leave off unless you know you want it.** Installs /usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-irq-rt + a boot service that re-chrt's the threads each boot. No-op if threadirqs isn't on the cmdline. `undo` removes the service and drops the threads back to SCHED_OTHER live.

After=multi-user.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStartPre=/usr/bin/sleep 5
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-irq-rt

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT

SteamClientIgpu.Description: Nobara/Fedora ship /usr/share/applications/steam.desktop with PrefersNonDefaultGPU=true + X-KDE-RunOnDiscreteGpu=true. On a muxless Optimus laptop (G15 5515 — the panel is wired to the iGPU) that launches the whole Steam *client* with the NVIDIA PRIME-offload environment, and the embedded-Chromium 'steamwebhelper' GPU subprocess then fails to initialise GL on the dGPU and aborts in a loop ('GPU process launch failed: error_code=1002 ... GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.', SIGTRAP) — you get no usable Steam window, just DrKonqi crash dialogs. This writes a user-level ~/.local/share/applications/steam.desktop shadow forcing both keys false so the client renders on the iGPU. Individual games still PRIME-offload to the NVIDIA GPU via their own launch options — only the store/library/friends UI moves. Fully quit and relaunch Steam from the app menu after applying. Reversible (removes the shadow).

KernelVerboseBoot.Content: Verbose boot — show the scrolling kernel + systemd log
KernelVerboseBoot.Description: Turns the boot into the classic full-detail scroll instead of the graphical splash. Drops 'quiet splash' and adds loglevel=7 (every kernel message on the console), printk.time=1 ([seconds] timestamp per line), systemd.show_status=1 + systemd.status_unit_format=combined (every 'Starting/Started <unit> - <description>' line), plymouth.enable=0. These only change what's DISPLAYED — kernel messages already live in a RAM ring buffer and systemd-journald captures the lot regardless, so there are no extra SSD writes. No disk encryption on this machine. Needs a reboot; fully reversible. Add 'systemd.log_level=debug' or 'debug' by hand for even more (that one does grow the journal).
apply: grubby --update-kernel=ALL --remove-args="quiet splash rhgb" --args="loglevel=7 printk.time=1 systemd.show_status=1 systemd.status_unit_format=combined plymouth.enable=0"
undo: grubby --update-kernel=ALL --remove-args="loglevel=7 printk.time=1 systemd.show_status=1 systemd.status_unit_format=combined plymouth.enable=0" --args="quiet splash"

NtfsForceMount.Content: NTFS data drives: mount even when Windows left them 'dirty'
NtfsForceMount.Description: Windows Fast Startup / hibernation leaves an NTFS volume marked dirty, and the kernel ntfs3 driver then REFUSES to mount it ('volume is dirty and force flag is not set') — with 'nofail' in fstab the boot just skips it, so on Linux the drive (and any Steam library / Proton prefixes on it) silently vanishes. This adds 'force' to the ntfs3 options for every NTFS line in /etc/fstab (kernel mounts it anyway; ntfs3 is journaling-aware so this is the normal fix), installs ntfs-3g for the 'ntfsfix' tool, clears the dirty bit on any currently-unmounted NTFS device, and remounts. Real cure: turn off 'Fast Startup' in Windows (Control Panel -> Power Options) so it stops happening. /etc/fstab backed up to /etc/fstab.tuxthrottle-bak; 'undo' restores it.
apply: for u in $(awk '$3=="ntfs3"{print $1}' /etc/fstab); do d=$(blkid -U "${u#UUID=}" 2>/dev/null || echo "$u"); [ -b "$d" ] && ! findmnt -S "$d" >/dev/null 2>&1 && ntfsfix -d "$d" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done

SteamAutostartMountWait.Content: Steam autostart: wait for external drives to mount first
SteamAutostartMountWait.Description: A 'nofail' external drive in /etc/fstab (an NTFS/exFAT Steam library, a Proton-prefix drive, ...) can still be mid-mount a few seconds after login, but a Steam autostart entry fires immediately — Steam then briefly logs 'Staging library folder not found' / 'Install library folder not found' for that library until the mount catches up (harmless once it does, but looks like a broken install in the meantime). This installs a small wrapper script and prefixes the Exec= line of ~/.config/autostart/steam.desktop with it, so Steam's autostart waits (up to 10s) for every 'nofail' fstab mountpoint to actually be mounted before launching. No-op if you have no 'nofail' drives, or no Steam autostart entry yet — enable Steam's own 'Start automatically' or the Game Tools low-resource-mode autostart first. autostart file backed up to steam.desktop.tuxthrottle-mountwait-bak (a separate backup from Steam low-resource mode's own, so the two don't clobber each other); 'undo' restores it.
apply: AS=/home/{USER}/.config/autostart/steam.desktop; if [ -f "$AS" ] && ! grep -q tuxthrottle-wait-mounts "$AS"; then cp -a "$AS" "$AS.tuxthrottle-mountwait-bak"; sed -i 's|^Exec=|Exec=/usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-wait-mounts |' "$AS"; fi
undo: AS=/home/{USER}/.config/autostart/steam.desktop; if [ -f "$AS.tuxthrottle-mountwait-bak" ]; then mv -f "$AS.tuxthrottle-mountwait-bak" "$AS"; elif [ -f "$AS" ]; then sed -i 's|^Exec=/usr/local/bin/tuxthrottle-wait-mounts |Exec=|' "$AS"; fi
